title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 324-325 of the 'équation des lacets' manuscript). π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, a free profinite group of rank 2. Ĝ^+_{0,3} is its extension by S_3 = G_3, the group permuting the three punctures, with lifts σ_∞ (an involution swapping 0 and 1) and ρ (order 3). L_0, L_1 are the loop (inertia) subgroups at 0 and 1, with σ_∞(L_0) = L_1 and ρ(L_0) = L_1. The task is to describe the outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} that preserve the loop structure and commute (outer) with S_3. Equivalently, these are automorphisms u of Ĝ^+_{0,3} that induce the identity on S_3, normalised by u(σ_∞) = σ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ. Here g ∈ π̂_{0,3} satisfies the cocycle condition (38), gρ(g)ρ²(g) = 1, which says (gρ)^3 = 1. The loop condition (39) asks for g_0 with u(L_0) = int(g_0)(L_0).

This page proves (40)/(41).
(i) Apply u to L_1 = ρ(L_0). Since u(ρ) = gρ, we get u(L_1) = int(gρ(g_0))(L_1); put g_1 = gρ(g_0).
(ii) Since u commutes with σ_∞, u(L_1) = σ_∞ u(L_0) = int(σ_∞(g_0))(L_1).
(iii) Hence σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g ρ(g_0) lies in the normaliser N(L_1). This normaliser equals L_1, because inertia subgroups of the free profinite group are self-normalising. So σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g ρ(g_0) = l_1^ν with ν ∈ Ẑ, which gives g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^ν ρ(g_0)^{-1}.

He then states the resulting parametrisation. The following are all equivalent data:
- an outer automorphism of π̂_{0,3} commuting with G_3 and preserving the conjugacy class of the loop subgroup L_0^! = ε_0^Ẑ;
- an automorphism u of Ĝ^+_{0,3} fixing σ_∞ and fixing ρ mod π̂_{0,3};
- a pair (g_0 mod L_0, ν ∈ Ẑ) satisfying (38), with g given by (40).

On the next page this yields int(g_0^{-1})u(ε_0) = ε_0^{2ν+1}, where ε_0 = σ_∞ρ and l_0 = ε_0^2. So the cyclotomic-type exponent is λ = 2ν+1.

This is Grothendieck's own route to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Fixing σ_∞ gives the 2-cycle relation, (38) is the order-3 ('hexagon') relation, and λ = 2ν+1 matches Drinfeld's m = (λ-1)/2. The factorisation g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^ν ρ(g_0)^{-1} expresses the GT element through the inertia conjugator g_0.
errors: (40) is cited above the equality u(L_1) = int(g_1)(L_1), but that step actually uses u(ρ) = gρ, i.e. (36), together with ρ(L_0) = L_1; (40) is the conclusion being proved, so the label is a slip.
The page uses ρ both for the order-3 element and, in (39) on the previous page, for an exponent in Ẑ^*. Writing u(L_0) = int(g_0)(L_0) without the exponent is harmless at the level of subgroups.

The remark that g does not depend on g_0 mod L_0 is trivially true, since g is defined by u alone. The substantive point is how ν changes when g_0 is replaced by g_0 l_0^a; this depends on the orientations σ_∞(l_0) = l_1^{±1} and ρ(l_0) = l_1^{±1}, which are not checked here (though the previous page claims ν is well determined).
The self-normalising property N(L_1) = L_1 in the free profinite group is used without proof. It is true but non-trivial in the profinite setting.

ideas.what: Describing loop-preserving outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} commuting with S_3 as automorphisms u of the S_3-extension Ĝ^+_{0,3}, with u(σ_∞) = σ_∞, u(ρ) = gρ and gρ(g)ρ²(g) = 1
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT-hat (2-cycle and 3-cycle relations); the S_3-orbifold version
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; Lochak–Schneps for the S_3/orbifold formulation
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and the action on π_{0,3}; La Longue Marche (1981) part one discusses π_{0,3} and S_3; this computation itself seems unpublished

ideas.what: Factorisation g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^ν ρ(g_0)^{-1}, where g_0 conjugates u(L_0) back to L_0
ideas.modern_name: Expressing the GT element f through inertia conjugators (coboundary-type description)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and Nakamura-style computations with inertia normalisers; Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Self-normalising property of inertia (loop) subgroups in the free profinite group of rank 2
Exponent of u on the orbifold loop ε_0 = σ_∞ρ equals 2ν+1, i.e. λ is odd and ν plays the role of m

missed.claim: This is an independent, pre-Drinfeld-style derivation of GT-type relations from the S_3-extension Ĝ^+_{0,3} and the loop condition. In it the integer m appears as ν, the inertia-at-1 exponent in g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^ν ρ(g_0)^{-1}. Its main interest is historical documentation of Grothendieck's own route rather than a new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck had the S_3-orbifold formulation of the GT relations, with the oddness of λ derived from the loop equation. This bears on attribution in histories of GT.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is routine, but it shows Grothendieck working out an essentially GT-hat-type parametrisation via the S_3-extension in unpublished notes. That is historically notable, though the mathematics itself is now standard.
transcription_corrections: In the line 'int(σ_∞(g_0)^{-1} g_1)(L_1) = L_1' the image shows '⊂ L_1', not '= L_1'.
In 'u σ_∞(L_0) = u(L_1) = int(g_1)(L_1)', the '40' written above refers to the second equality.
'défini en termes de u {+et de σ+}': the insertion above the line reads 'et de σ', followed by a check mark.

'ou encore celle d'un automorphisme intérieur [?] u_0' is doubtful. The image reads roughly 'ou encore celle d'un automorphisme u_0 de π̂_{0,3} commutant à σ_∞, et cat.t [?] à ρ'; 'intérieur' seems spurious, and the context suggests '(extérieurement) à ρ'.
'— équivaut [?] :' at the start of the last lines is probably 'Équivalemment :'.
